```text
CREATE TABLE workers (
  id text PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL,
  run_id text NOT NULL,
  type text NOT NULL,
  status text NOT NULL,
  cwd text NOT NULL,
  created_at integer NOT NULL,
  updated_at integer NOT NULL, output_log text NOT NULL DEFAULT '', bridge_session_id text, bridge_session_mode text, output_entries_json text NOT NULL DEFAULT '', current_text text NOT NULL DEFAULT '', last_text text NOT NULL DEFAULT '', title text NOT NULL DEFAULT '', initial_prompt text NOT NULL DEFAULT '', worker_number integer, active_work_started_at integer, active_work_duration_ms integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, worker_role text, allocation_key text, turn_generation integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, effective_launch_model text, effective_launch_effort text, launch_credential_source text, superseded_from_seq integer, superseded_seq_ranges text,
  FOREIGN KEY (run_id) REFERENCES runs(id) ON UPDATE no action ON DELETE no action
);
CREATE INDEX workers_run_idx ON workers(run_id);
CREATE TRIGGER workers_work_timer_insert
AFTER INSERT ON workers
WHEN lower(substr(NEW.status, 1, instr(NEW.status || ':', ':') - 1)) = 'working'
BEGIN
  UPDATE workers
  SET active_work_started_at = COALESCE(NEW.active_work_started_at, NEW.created_at),
      active_work_duration_ms = COALESCE(NEW.active_work_duration_ms, 0)
  WHERE id = NEW.id;
END;
CREATE TRIGGER workers_work_timer_start
AFTER UPDATE OF status, updated_at ON workers
WHEN lower(substr(OLD.status, 1, instr(OLD.status || ':', ':') - 1)) != 'working'
  AND lower(substr(NEW.status, 1, instr(NEW.status || ':', ':') - 1)) = 'working'
BEGIN
  UPDATE workers
  SET active_work_started_at = NEW.updated_at,
      active_work_duration_ms = COALESCE(NEW.active_work_duration_ms, OLD.active_work_duration_ms, 0)
  WHERE id = NEW.id;
END;
CREATE TRIGGER workers_work_timer_stop
AFTER UPDATE OF status, updated_at ON workers
WHEN lower(substr(OLD.status, 1, instr(OLD.status || ':', ':') - 1)) = 'working'
  AND lower(substr(NEW.status, 1, instr(NEW.status || ':', ':') - 1)) != 'working'
BEGIN
  UPDATE workers
  SET active_work_started_at = NULL,
      active_work_duration_ms = COALESCE(OLD.active_work_duration_ms, 0)
        + (MAX(0, NEW.updated_at - COALESCE(OLD.active_work_started_at, OLD.updated_at, OLD.created_at, NEW.updated_at)) * 1000)
  WHERE id = NEW.id;
END;
CREATE INDEX workers_run_created_id_idx ON workers(run_id, created_at, id);
CREATE INDEX workers_created_id_idx ON workers(created_at, id);
---
CREATE TABLE recovery_incidents (
  id text PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL,
  run_id text NOT NULL,
  worker_id text,
  queued_message_id text,
  kind text NOT NULL,
  status text NOT NULL,
  auto_attempt_count integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  last_error text,
  details text,
  detected_at integer NOT NULL,
  updated_at integer NOT NULL,
  resolved_at integer,
  FOREIGN KEY (run_id) REFERENCES runs(id) ON UPDATE no action ON DELETE no action,
  FOREIGN KEY (worker_id) REFERENCES workers(id) ON UPDATE no action ON DELETE no action,
  FOREIGN KEY (queued_message_id) REFERENCES queued_conversation_messages(id) ON UPDATE no action ON DELETE no action
);
CREATE INDEX recovery_incidents_run_status_updated_idx ON recovery_incidents(run_id, status, updated_at);
CREATE INDEX recovery_incidents_run_updated_id_desc_idx ON recovery_incidents(run_id, updated_at DESC, id DESC);

CREATE TABLE execution_events (
  id text PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL,
  run_id text NOT NULL,
  worker_id text,

  event_type text NOT NULL,
  details text,
  created_at integer NOT NULL, artifact_seq integer, details_hash text, details_preview text,

);
CREATE INDEX execution_events_run_created_idx ON execution_events(run_id, created_at);
CREATE INDEX execution_events_run_created_id_desc_idx ON execution_events(run_id, created_at DESC, id DESC);

1	import { randomUUID } from "crypto";
2	import { recordExecutionEvent } from "@/server/events/execution-event-store";
3	import { and, eq, inArray } from "drizzle-orm";
4	import { db } from "@/server/db";
5	import { recoveryIncidents } from "@/server/db/schema";
6	import { emitNamedEvent } from "@/server/events/named-events";
7	
8	export type RecoveryIncidentKind = "worker_lost" | "session_missing" | "queue_blocked" | "stale_running" | "quota_exhausted";
9	export type RecoveryIncidentStatus = "open" | "recovering" | "resolved" | "needs_user" | "failed";
10	
11	const OPEN_INCIDENT_STATUSES: RecoveryIncidentStatus[] = ["open", "recovering", "needs_user"];
12	
13	function serializeDetails(details: Record<string, unknown> | null | undefined) {
14	  return details ? JSON.stringify(details) : null;
15	}
16	
17	function parseDetails(details: string | null | undefined): Record<string, unknown> {
18	  if (!details) {
19	    return {};
20	  }
21	  try {
22	    const parsed: unknown = JSON.parse(details);
23	    return parsed && typeof parsed === "object" && !Array.isArray(parsed)
24	      ? parsed as Record<string, unknown>
25	      : {};
26	  } catch {
27	    return {};
28	  }
29	}
30	
31	async function insertRecoveryEvent(
32	  runId: string,
33	  workerId: string | null | undefined,
34	  eventType: string,
35	  details: Record<string, unknown>,
36	) {
37	  await recordExecutionEvent({
38	    runId,
39	    workerId: workerId ?? null,
40	    planItemId: null,
41	    eventType,
42	    details,
43	  });
44	}
45	
46	async function findOpenIncident(args: {
47	  runId: string;
48	  workerId?: string | null;
49	  queuedMessageId?: string | null;
50	  kind: RecoveryIncidentKind;
51	}) {
52	  const records = await db
53	    .select()
54	    .from(recoveryIncidents)
55	    .where(and(
56	      eq(recoveryIncidents.runId, args.runId),
57	      eq(recoveryIncidents.kind, args.kind),
58	      inArray(recoveryIncidents.status, OPEN_INCIDENT_STATUSES),
59	    ));
60	
61	  return records.find((record) => (
62	    (record.workerId ?? null) === (args.workerId ?? null)
63	    && (record.queuedMessageId ?? null) === (args.queuedMessageId ?? null)
64	  )) ?? null;
65	}
66	
67	export async function openRecoveryIncident(args: {
68	  runId: string;
69	  workerId?: string | null;
70	  queuedMessageId?: string | null;
71	  kind: RecoveryIncidentKind;
72	  details?: Record<string, unknown>;
73	  lastError?: string | null;
74	}) {
75	  const existing = await findOpenIncident(args);
76	  const now = new Date();
77	  if (existing) {
78	    const details = { ...parseDetails(existing.details), ...(args.details ?? {}) };
79	    await db.update(recoveryIncidents).set({
80	      details: serializeDetails(details),
81	      lastError: args.lastError ?? existing.lastError,
82	      updatedAt: now,
83	    }).where(eq(recoveryIncidents.id, existing.id));
84	    return { ...existing, details: serializeDetails(details), updatedAt: now };
85	  }
86	
87	  const record = {
88	    id: randomUUID(),
89	    runId: args.runId,
90	    workerId: args.workerId ?? null,
91	    queuedMessageId: args.queuedMessageId ?? null,
92	    kind: args.kind,
93	    status: "open" as const,
94	    autoAttemptCount: 0,
95	    lastError: args.lastError ?? null,
96	    details: serializeDetails(args.details),
97	    detectedAt: now,
98	    updatedAt: now,
99	    resolvedAt: null,
100	  };
101	
102	  await db.insert(recoveryIncidents).values(record);
103	  await insertRecoveryEvent(args.runId, args.workerId, "recovery_incident_opened", {
104	    summary: `Opened ${args.kind} recovery incident.`,
105	    incidentId: record.id,
106	    kind: args.kind,
107	    queuedMessageId: args.queuedMessageId ?? null,

529	export async function reconcileRunRecovery(args: {
530	  runId: string;
531	  liveAgents: RecoveryLiveAgentLike[];
532	  force?: boolean;
533	  source?: string;
534	}) {
535	  const { run, runWorkers, runMessages, runQueuedMessages } = await loadRunRecoveryInputs(args.runId);
536	  const state = classifyRunRecoveryState({
537	    run,
538	    workers: runWorkers,
539	    liveAgents: args.liveAgents,
540	    messages: runMessages,
541	    queuedMessages: runQueuedMessages,
542	  });
543	
544	  if (state.kind === "healthy" || state.kind === "recovering") {
545	    return { action: "none" as const, runId: run.id, recoveryState: state };
546	  }
547	
548	  if (state.kind === "needs_recovery" && run.status === "needs_recovery" && !args.force) {
549	    return { action: "needs_user" as const, runId: run.id, recoveryState: state };
550	  }
551	
552	  if (run.mode === "implementation" && normalizeRunStatus(run.status) === "awaiting_user") {
553	    await recordRecoveryPausedForUser({
554	      runId: run.id,
555	      workerId: state.workerId,
556	      state,
557	      source: args.source,
558	    });
559	    notifyEventStreamSubscribers();
560	    return { action: "none" as const, runId: run.id, recoveryState: state };
561	  }
562	
563	  const incident = await openRecoveryIncident({
564	    runId: run.id,
565	    workerId: state.workerId,
566	    queuedMessageId: state.queuedMessageId,
567	    kind: incidentKindForState(state),
568	    lastError: state.reason ?? null,
569	    details: {
570	      source: args.source ?? "reconciler",
571	      recoveryState: state.kind,
572	      recommendedAction: state.recommendedAction,
573	      reason: state.reason ?? null,
574	    },
575	  });
576	  const policy = await getRecoveryPolicy();
577	  const decision = decideRecoveryAction({
578	    runMode: run.mode,
579	    recoveryState: state,
580	    policy,
581	    autoAttemptCount: incident.autoAttemptCount,
582	    force: args.force,
583	  });
584	  if (decision.action === "needs_user") {
585	    await markNeedsUser({
586	      incidentId: incident.id,
587	      runId: run.id,
588	      workerId: state.workerId,
589	      reason: decision.reason,
590	      state,
591	    });
592	    notifyEventStreamSubscribers();
593	    return { action: "needs_user" as const, runId: run.id, recoveryState: state };
594	  }
595	
596	  if (decision.action === "wait_for_quota_reset") {
597	    return {
598	      action: "wait_for_quota_reset" as const,
599	      runId: run.id,
600	      recoveryState: state,
601	      resumeAt: decision.resumeAt,
602	    };
603	  }
604	
605	  const nextAttemptAt = incident.autoAttemptCount > 0 && !args.force
606	    ? computeRecoveryBackoff({
607	      policy,
608	      attemptCount: incident.autoAttemptCount,
609	      nowMs: incident.updatedAt.getTime(),
610	    })
611	    : null;
612	  if (nextAttemptAt && nextAttemptAt.getTime() > Date.now()) {
613	    await insertRecoveryExecutionEvent(run.id, state.workerId, "recovery_backoff_scheduled", {
614	      summary: "Recovery is waiting for its retry backoff window.",
615	      incidentId: incident.id,
616	      nextAttemptAt: nextAttemptAt.toISOString(),
617	    });
618	    return { action: "wait_for_backoff" as const, runId: run.id, recoveryState: state, nextAttemptAt };
619	  }
620	
621	  try {
622	    if (decision.action === "resume_session") {
623	      const worker = runWorkers.find((candidate) => candidate.id === state.workerId);
624	      if (!worker) {
625	        throw new Error("Recoverable worker not found");
626	      }
627	      const result = await resumeSavedWorkerSession({ run, worker, state, incidentId: incident.id });
628	      notifyEventStreamSubscribers();
629	      return { ...result, recoveryState: state };
630	    }
631	
632	    if (decision.action === "restart_from_checkpoint") {
633	      const result = await restartFromCheckpoint({
634	        run,
635	        workerId: state.workerId,
636	        state,
637	        incidentId: incident.id,
638	        preserveQueuedMessages: policy.preserveQueuedMessages,
639	      });
640	      notifyEventStreamSubscribers();
641	      return { ...result, recoveryState: state };
642	    }
643	
644	    if (decision.action === "mark_failed") {
645	      await markRecoveryIncidentFailed({
646	        incidentId: incident.id,
647	        runId: run.id,
648	        workerId: state.workerId,
649	        reason: decision.reason,
650	        details: { recoveryState: state.kind },
651	      });
652	      notifyEventStreamSubscribers();
653	      return { action: "failed" as const, runId: run.id, recoveryState: state };
654	    }
655	
656	    return { action: "none" as const, runId: run.id, recoveryState: state };
657	  } catch (error) {
658	    const reason = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
659	    if (
660	      isRecoverableAgentMissingError(reason)
661	      && state.kind === "lost_worker_resumable"
662	      && run.mode === "implementation"
663	      && policy.restartFromCheckpointWhenSessionMissing
664	    ) {
665	      try {
666	        const restartResult = await restartFromCheckpoint({
667	          run,
668	          workerId: state.workerId,
669	          state: { ...state, kind: "lost_worker_rerunnable", sessionId: null },
670	          incidentId: incident.id,
671	          preserveQueuedMessages: policy.preserveQueuedMessages,
672	        });
673	        notifyEventStreamSubscribers();
674	        return { ...restartResult, recoveryState: state };
675	      } catch (restartError) {
676	        const restartReason = restartError instanceof Error ? restartError.message : String(restartError);
677	        await markNeedsUser({
678	          incidentId: incident.id,
679	          runId: run.id,
680	          workerId: state.workerId,
681	          reason: restartReason,
682	          state,
683	        });
684	        notifyEventStreamSubscribers();
685	        return { action: "needs_user" as const, runId: run.id, recoveryState: state };
686	      }
687	    }
688	
689	    await markNeedsUser({
690	      incidentId: incident.id,
691	      runId: run.id,
692	      workerId: state.workerId,
693	      reason,
694	      state,
695	    });
696	    notifyEventStreamSubscribers();
697	    return { action: "needs_user" as const, runId: run.id, recoveryState: state };
698	  }
699	}

#!/usr/bin/env node
import { createAgentRuntimeServer } from "../src/server/agent-runtime/http";

const port = Number(process.env.OMNIHARNESS_AGENT_RUNTIME_PORT || "7800");
const host = process.env.OMNIHARNESS_AGENT_RUNTIME_HOST || "127.0.0.1";

const server = createAgentRuntimeServer({
  env: process.env,
});

server.listen(port, host, () => {
  process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({
    ok: true,
    event: "listening",
    host,
    port,
    runtime: "omniharness-agent-runtime",
  }) + "\n");
});

function shutdown() {
  server.close(() => process.exit(0));
  setTimeout(() => process.exit(0), 1000).unref();
}

process.on("SIGINT", shutdown);
process.on("SIGTERM", shutdown);

## Claude · 2026-08-03T07:01:25.007Z

I dug into the DB, the runner log, and the live bridge. Here's what actually happened — and the premise is partly different from what the UI told you.

## `b5fef7f771eb` was not stuck. It was running, and the banner lied.

Timeline from `execution_events` + `recovery_incidents`:

| time | event |
|---|---|
| 08:46:26 | conversation-sync detects `session_missing`; incident opened, policy → `resume_session` |
| 08:46:27 | session resumed OK; `recovery_continuation_started` — injects the "runner restarted, resume the interrupted task" prompt |
| 08:46:43 | your answer to the old question → **409 `no_pending_elicitations`** (elicitation died with the old session) |
| 08:47:54 | you re-send the form → queued (`decision: drain`, `reason: pending_elicitation`) |
| 08:57:39 | continuation turn finally finishes → incident `resolved`, run → `done`; **`queued_message_failed` — "delivered 0 of 1"** |

The resume succeeded in **1 second**. What took 11 minutes was the injected continuation turn — a normal working turn. But `resumeSavedWorkerSession` hands incident resolution to the background continuation (`recovery-reconciler.ts:460-471`), so the incident sits at `status='recovering'` for the whole turn, and the banner keeps rendering `recovery.notice.description.recovering` — "restoring the worker session…, Attempts: 1". Recovery was done; only the turn was running. **The banner reports the wrong phase.**

And your re-sent answer was **dropped** — that's the real damage, not a cosmetic issue.

## `73fe3ee52059` is the genuinely stuck one — and it's an auth bug

Its ACP stderr is a wall of:
```
Internal error: Failed to authenticate. API Error: 401 OAuth access token has been revoked.
```
The bridge surfaces that as HTTP 500. `RETRYABLE_STATUS_CODES` (`retry.ts:1`) contains 500, and `PERMANENT_MESSAGE_PATTERNS` only matches `authentication required` / `API key not valid` — neither matches "Failed to authenticate" or "OAuth access token has been revoked". So **a revoked token is classified transient**: recovery retried 3× per attempt, every ~15s, from 08:32:47 to 08:38:56, each ending in a 500 to the UI. You were never told to re-authenticate.

## Bonus: the context meter is broken

Every live agent reports `fullnessPercent: 100`. `b5fef7f771eb` had `inputTokens: 12873, outputTokens: 34456` but `totalTokens: 11160656` against `maxTokens: 200000`. `applyPromptUsage` (`manager.ts:426`) writes a **cumulative session token count** into `totalTokens`, the same field `applySessionUsageUpdate` uses for **live context size**. Last writer wins, so once a prompt-usage event lands, the meter pins to 100% permanently.

Right now all four runs have converged on their own (`done` / `awaiting_user` / `running`) and no incidents are open — so there's nothing to unstick, but four real bugs to fix.

/**
 * Closing out human-input requests that the runtime no longer holds.
 *
 * Elicitations and permissions live in two places: the runtime's in-memory
 * `pendingElicitations`/`pendingPermissions` (the promise the agent is blocked
 * on) and the durable worker stream (an append-only `pending` row, later
 * superseded by a terminal row). Every UI surface derives "is this question
 * still open?" from the stream, because `/api/events` strips
 * `agent.outputEntries` and a live snapshot does not always carry the pending
 * arrays.
 *
 * The two can diverge: if the runtime process dies, or a worker is torn down
 * and respawned, the in-memory request disappears without a terminal row ever
 * being written. The stream then advertises a question forever — the user

  "old_string": "function applyPromptUsage(record: AgentRecord, usage: unknown) {\n  const payload = asRecord(usage);\n  if (!payload) {\n    return;\n  }\n\n  updateContextUsage(record, {\n    inputTokens: finiteNumber(payload.inputTokens),\n    outputTokens: finiteNumber(payload.outputTokens),\n    totalTokens: finiteNumber(payload.totalTokens),\n  });\n}",
  "new_string": "/**\n * Per-turn usage from a prompt response. Its `totalTokens` is a cumulative spend\n * counter for the whole session, not the live context size — a long session\n * reports millions against a 200k window. `contextUsage.totalTokens` means\n * \"tokens currently in context\" and drives `fullnessPercent`, so letting prompt\n * usage write it pinned every long-running agent to 100% full forever.\n *\n * Only `session/update` usage (`used`/`size`, via `applySessionUsageUpdate`)\n * measures the live window, and it is the sole source of `maxTokens`. So once a\n * window is known, leave the context fields to it and record spend only.\n */\nfunction applyPromptUsage(record: AgentRecord, usage: unknown) {\n  const payload = asRecord(usage);\n  if (!payload) {\n    return;\n  }\n\n  const hasSessionReportedWindow = finiteNumber(record.contextUsage?.maxTokens) !== null;\n  updateContextUsage(record, {\n    inputTokens: finiteNumber(payload.inputTokens),\n    outputTokens: finiteNumber(payload.outputTokens),\n    ...(hasSessionReportedWindow ? {} : { totalTokens: finiteNumber(payload.totalTokens) }),\n  });\n}"
}

describe("isTransientSupervisorError", () => {

  });

    expect(isTransientSupervisorError(new Error("Agent runtime list request timed out after 5000ms."))).toBe(true);
  });

    expect(isTransientSupervisorError(new Error("Cannot connect to API: connect ETIMEDOUT api.example.com"))).toBe(true);
  });

    expect(isTransientSupervisorError(Object.assign(new Error("Timed out waiting for worker output lock: /tmp/worker.jsonl.lock"), {
      code: "ELOCKED",
    }))).toBe(true);
    expect(isTransientSupervisorError(new Error("Lock file is already being held"))).toBe(true);

async function waitForProcessExit(pid: number) {
  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 20; attempt += 1) {
    try {
      process.kill(pid, 0);
    } catch {
      return true;
    }
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 50));
  }
  return false;
}

export type RecoverRunAction = "retry" | "edit" | "fork";

export function shouldSelectRecoveredRunAfterSuccess({
  action,
  currentSelectedRunId,
  requestedRunId,
  recoveredRunId,
}: {
  action: RecoverRunAction;
  currentSelectedRunId: string | null;
  requestedRunId: string;
  recoveredRunId: string | null | undefined;
}) {
  if (!recoveredRunId) {
    return false;
  }

  if (action === "fork") {
    return true;
  }

  return currentSelectedRunId === requestedRunId;
}

export function cancelInactiveAutoResumeTimers<TEntry extends { timerId: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null }>(
  entries: Map<string, TEntry>,
  activeRunId: string | null,
  clearTimer: (timerId: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>) => void = clearTimeout,
) {
  let cancelled = 0;

  for (const [runId, entry] of entries.entries()) {
    if (runId === activeRunId) {
      continue;
    }

    if (entry.timerId) {
      clearTimer(entry.timerId);
      cancelled += 1;
    }
    entries.delete(runId);
  }

  return cancelled;
}

export function isPermanentAutoResumeFailure(failureKey: string | null | undefined) {
  return /\b(?:api key|authentication required|auth(?:entication)? failed|billing required|api billing|cap_exceeded|insufficient quota|resource exhausted|system resources are low|worker\.spawn\.resource_exhausted)\b/i.test(failureKey ?? "");
}

export function shouldFireAutoResumeTimer<TEntry extends {
  failureKey: string;
  targetMessageId: string;
  timerId: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null;
}>(args: {
  entries: Map<string, TEntry>;
  runId: string;
  failureKey: string;
  targetMessageId: string;
  activeRunId: string | null;

## Claude · 2026-08-03T07:32:05.591Z

All five fixes are in, tests and typecheck pass. Now your questions, answered from the code and the data.

## First: what run `70fc72a5667b` did

At **09:27:10** it fired a milestone auto-commit (`auto_commit_milestones=1`, `push_on_commit=1`), swept the **entire dirty working tree** into commit `2e6d9a8` — your pre-existing uncommitted changes, my in-flight fixes, and a large pile of `apps/*/node_modules/.vite` build artifacts — and **pushed it to GitHub**. `git ls-remote` confirms `2e6d9a8` is on `origin/refs/heads/master`, and the reflog records it as "update by push". It failed ~35 seconds later with `403 Account suspended`.

I have not touched that commit or the remote — reverting a pushed commit on `master` is your call. Say the word and I'll do it.

## "If I delete it, will everything stop?"

Yes, for that run. `runs.ts:797-820` does: `requestConversationDeletion` → `cancelSupervisorWake` → `stopRunObserver` → `cancelAgent()` on every worker → then deletes the records. It genuinely tears the run down.

But it is **not instant**: line 821 does `await waitForConversationBackgroundTasks(runId)` — delete blocks until every server-owned turn for that run unwinds. That's exactly the "stop isn't authoritative" behaviour you're describing.

## "It tries to resume when I open it — it never should"

Found it, and it's the same root cause as the server-side bug. `isPermanentAutoResumeFailure` (`auto-resume-selection.ts`) gates auto-resume, and its pattern list had `auth(entication)? failed` — but the adapter's actual wording is **"Failed to authenticate. API Error: 403 Account suspended"**: reversed word order, and `account suspended` wasn't listed at all. So the guard returned `false` and the UI re-armed auto-resume every time you opened the conversation.

## What I fixed

| # | Bug | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Recovery banner claimed "restoring worker" for the entire post-recovery turn (11 min on `b5fef7f771eb`) | Incident resolves when the session is back, not when the continuation turn ends; failure reopens it and clears `resolvedAt` |
| 2 | Your re-sent answer silently dropped (`queued_message_failed`, "delivered 0 of 1") | `no_pending_elicitations` now closes the stale card and falls through to normal prompt delivery instead of failing the row |
| 3 | Revoked/suspended credentials classified as transient (HTTP 500), so recovery span on them | Added the real adapter wordings to `PERMANENT_MESSAGE_PATTERNS` |
| 4 | Context meter pinned at 100% (cumulative spend written into the live-window field) | Prompt usage no longer overwrites `totalTokens` once a session-reported window exists |
| 5 | Opening a permanently-failed session re-fires auto-resume | Same wordings added to `isPermanentAutoResumeFailure` |

Tests: 58 passing across the four affected suites plus 35 in the runtime HTTP suite; `tsconfig.runner.json` and `tsconfig.interface.json` both clean. Each fix has a regression test, and I confirmed the drain test fails without fix 2 (it caught the behaviour change immediately).

## What I have **not** done

Your core demand — **stop must be instant, unskippable, and authoritative for any action** — is a design change I haven't made. Today stop is best-effort and awaits background tasks. Doing it properly means a run-scoped abort signal that every turn, drain, recovery continuation, and auto-commit checks and honours immediately, with the DB flipped to cancelled *before* waiting on anything. That's a real piece of work, not a patch — I didn't want to half-do it inside this turn.

Two things I'd suggest deciding now: whether to revert/clean `2e6d9a8` on the remote, and whether to disable `auto_commit_milestones`/`push_on_commit` on runs whose project path is the OmniHarness repo itself. Want me to take on the stop-authority work next?

export function isWorkerTurnSupersededError(error: unknown): boolean {
  const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
  return /\bworker turn (?:was )?superseded by a newer worker turn\b/i.test(message);
}

function runOnChain<T>(
  chains: Map<string, Promise<void>>,
  key: string,
  task: () => Promise<T>,
): Promise<T> {
  const previous = chains.get(key) ?? Promise.resolve();
  const next = previous.then(() => task());
  const tracked = next.then(() => undefined, () => undefined);
  chains.set(key, tracked);
  return next.finally(() => {
    if (chains.get(key) === tracked) {
      chains.delete(key);
    }
  });
}

export function runWorkerTurn<T>(workerId: string, task: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
  return runOnChain(workerTurnChains, workerId, task);
}

/**
 * Read the worker's current turn fence value. Returns 0 when the worker
 * row is missing (treated as the default generation).
 */
export async function readWorkerTurnGeneration(workerId: string): Promise<number> {
  const record = await db
    .select({ turnGeneration: workers.turnGeneration })
    .from(workers)
    .where(eq(workers.id, workerId))
    .get();
  return record?.turnGeneration ?? 0;
}

/**
 * Capture a worker turn generation when the worker exists. A null result means
 * the bridge request is not backed by a persisted conversation worker and
 * therefore cannot participate in the database turn fence.
 */
export async function captureWorkerTurnGeneration(workerId: string): Promise<number | null> {
  const record = await db
    .select({ turnGeneration: workers.turnGeneration })
    .from(workers)
    .where(eq(workers.id, workerId))
    .get();
  return record?.turnGeneration ?? null;
}

/**

 * worker state into a delivery-safe shape in the SAME mutation, so an
 * immediate queued delivery cannot observe stale `working` state after a
 * successful cancel. Returns the new generation value.
 *
 * Callers capture the returned generation for the new delivery; any older
 * in-flight completion that captured a smaller value must refuse to persist
 * terminal updates (see `isWorkerTurnGenerationCurrent`).
 */
export async function advanceWorkerTurnGeneration(
  workerId: string,
  reset?: { status?: string; clearCurrentText?: boolean; updatedAt?: Date },
): Promise<number> {
  await db.update(workers).set({
    turnGeneration: sql`${workers.turnGeneration} + 1`,
    ...(reset?.status !== undefined ? { status: reset.status } : {}),
    ...(reset?.clearCurrentText ? { currentText: "" } : {}),
    ...(reset?.updatedAt ? { updatedAt: reset.updatedAt } : {}),
  }).where(eq(workers.id, workerId));
  return readWorkerTurnGeneration(workerId);
}

/**
 * True when `capturedGeneration` still matches the worker's persisted fence,

export async function isWorkerTurnGenerationCurrent(
  workerId: string,
  capturedGeneration: number,
): Promise<boolean> {
  const record = await db
    .select({ turnGeneration: workers.turnGeneration })
    .from(workers)
    .where(eq(workers.id, workerId))
    .get();
  if (!record) {
    return false;
  }
  return record.turnGeneration === capturedGeneration;
}

export async function interruptWithDraftMessage(params: {
  runId: string;
  content: string;
  attachments?: ChatAttachment[];
  targetWorkerId?: string | null;
  source?: InterruptSource;
}): Promise<InterruptResult> {
  const run = await loadRun(params.runId);
  const trimmed = params.content.trim();
  const normalizedAttachments = normalizeChatAttachments(params.attachments ?? []);
  if (!trimmed && normalizedAttachments.length === 0) {
    emitNamedEvent({
      kind: "queue.interrupt_refused",
      runId: params.runId,
      workerId: params.targetWorkerId ?? null,
      queuedMessageId: null,
      reason: "no_user_intent",
      source: params.source ?? "escape",
    });
    throw refusal(400, "Message content or attachment is required");
  }

  // Persist the draft as exactly one queued row, then deliver that same id.
  const created = await createQueuedConversationMessage({
    runId: params.runId,
    targetWorkerId: params.targetWorkerId ?? null,
    action: "steer",
    content: params.content,
    attachments: normalizedAttachments,
  });
  const record = await loadQueuedRecord(params.runId, created.id);
  return interruptAndDeliver({ run, record, source: params.source ?? "escape" });
}

  private async runAgentRequest<T>(record: AgentRecord, request: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
    assertAgentCanReceiveRequest(record);
    return await new Promise<T>((resolve, reject) => {
      const rejectForExit = (code: number | null, signal: NodeJS.Signals | null) => {
        const message = `Agent is not running: ${record.name} (exit code=${code} signal=${signal})`;
        record.state = "stopped";
        record.lastError = record.lastError ?? `exit code=${code} signal=${signal}`;
        record.updatedAt = nowIso();
        reject(new RuntimeHttpError(409, message));
      };
      const rejectForError = (error: Error) => {
        const message = `Agent process error: ${error.message}`;
        record.state = "error";
        record.lastError = message;
        record.updatedAt = nowIso();
        reject(new RuntimeHttpError(500, message));
      };
      const cleanup = () => {
        record.child.off("exit", rejectForExit);
        record.child.off("error", rejectForError);
      };

      record.child.once("exit", rejectForExit);
      record.child.once("error", rejectForError);
      suppressClosedPipeAcpWriteConsoleError(request).then(resolve, reject).finally(cleanup);
    });
  }

  async startAgent(input: StartAgentInput) {
    this.lastAgentUseAt = Date.now();
    const type = input.type?.trim() || "opencode";

## Claude · 2026-08-03T07:40:19.027Z

Understood — and to be clear: **stop will not delete anything.** Delete is a separate explicit action you don't have to use; what I described was only what the delete endpoint does today. Nothing in the stop path removes records.

Here's why stop and steer are slow today. All four verified in code:

**1. There is no abort path at all.** `grep AbortController|AbortSignal src/server/bridge-client/` returns **zero hits**. `askAgent` does a plain `fetch` and reads the SSE stream to completion. Nothing can tear that stream down — cancel doesn't, because it can't.

**2. `runWorkerTurn` is a strict FIFO promise chain** (`worker-turn-gate.ts:17-34`). Your steer is enqueued *behind* the very turn it just cancelled, so it can't start until that turn's promise settles — which requires #1. That's your "message bouncing between sent and queued".

**3. The steer request blocks on the adapter.** `interruptAndDeliver` does `await cancelAgentTurn(worker.id)` (`queued-message-interrupt.ts:190`) — an HTTP round trip to the bridge, then a JSON-RPC round trip to the agent — before the UI hears anything. A wedged adapter (like your 401-spinning ones) blocks the button indefinitely.

**4. `askAgent` retries "indefinitely"** on connection errors (`retryIndefinitelyWhen`), so a failing turn can re-enter and hold the chain even longer.

And: the Claude adapter advertises `promptQueueing: true` in its capabilities — OmniHarness never uses it. Zero hits in `src/`.

## The fix: make the DB fence authoritative, the network best-effort

The good news is the correctness machinery already exists — `advanceWorkerTurnGeneration` / `isWorkerTurnGenerationCurrent` already make stale turns' writes no-ops. It's just used in the wrong order.

- **Stop:** flip persisted state *first* (advance fence, status → cancelled, clear text) — instant and authoritative, before any I/O. Abort the in-flight turn locally via a per-worker `AbortController` wired through `askAgent` → `fetch` → SSE reader. Fire `session/cancel` at the adapter as `void`, never awaited. A wedged adapter can no longer make stop slow.
- **Steer:** `runWorkerTurn` gains preemption — abort the current turn and start the new one *immediately* instead of chaining behind it. With that, a steer never falls back into the queue, so the sent/queued bouncing disappears structurally.
- **Delete:** drop `await waitForConversationBackgroundTasks` from the user's path (aborted turns can't write anyway, thanks to the fence).

One decision is genuinely yours, because it changes what steer *means*:

Before the abort path existed this could only end when the agent\n    // decided to end it, so stop and steer had to wait for it.\n    const wedgedTurn = runWorkerTurn(\"worker-wedged\", (signal) => new Promise((_resolve, reject) => {\n      signal.addEventListener(\"abort\", () => reject(signal.reason), { once: true });\n    }));\n\n    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 5));\n    expect(hasLiveWorkerTurn(\"worker-wedged\")).toBe(true);\n\n    const abortedAt = Date.now();\n    expect(abortWorkerTurn(\"worker-wedged\", \"user stop\")).toBe(true);\n    await expect(wedgedTurn).rejects.toSatisfy(isWorkerTurnAbortedError);\n    expect(Date.now() - abortedAt).toBeLessThan(200);\n    expect(hasLiveWorkerTurn(\"worker-wedged\")).toBe(false);\n  });\n\n  it(\"lets the next turn start immediately after the previous one is aborted\", async () => {\n    __resetWorkerTurnAbortsForTests();\n    const wedgedTurn = runWorkerTurn(\"worker-replace\", (signal) => new Promise((_resolve, reject) => {\n      signal.addEventListener(\"abort\", () => reject(signal.reason), { once: true });\n    }));\n    wedgedTurn.catch(() => undefined);\n    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 5));\n\n    // This is what steer does: abort, then deliver the replacement turn.\n    const requestedAt = Date.now();\n    abortWorkerTurn(\"worker-replace\", \"user steer\");\n    const replacement = await runWorkerTurn(\"worker-replace\", async () => \"replacement ran\");\n\n    expect(replacement).toBe(\"replacement ran\");\n    expect(Date.now() - ## Claude · 2026-08-03T07:54:54.527Z

**373 files, 2406 tests passing, all four typecheck projects clean.**

## STOP and STEER are now instant

The core problem was that **nothing could end a running turn**. `grep AbortController|AbortSignal src/server/bridge-client/` returned zero hits — `askAgent` read its SSE stream to completion, so a "cancel" could only *ask* the agent to stop and then wait. Everything else followed from that.

**What I added** — an abort signal published on an `AsyncLocalStorage` by `runWorkerTurn`, so it reaches `askAgent` however deeply nested, without threading a parameter through dozens of call sites:

```
abortWorkerTurn(workerId)   // synchronous, local, no I/O
  → trips the turn's AbortSignal
  → fetch aborts + SSE reader.cancel()  → the turn dies now
  → chain drains → replacement turn starts immediately
```

**Stop** (`cancelWorker`): aborts the turn locally, then advances the turn fence to `cancelled` in one mutation. `session/cancel` goes to the agent as `void` — never awaited. A wedged adapter can no longer delay stop by even a tick.

**Steer** (`interruptAndDeliver`): same code path, exactly as you chose. It used to `await cancelAgentTurn(...)` — an HTTP round trip *plus* a JSON-RPC round trip — before the UI heard anything, and threw **502 "Could not interrupt the active turn"** if that failed. Both are gone: the local abort is authoritative, the agent-side cancel is a courtesy.

**The queue bouncing** is fixed at the root. `askAgent` retried "indefinitely" on connection errors, and an abort *looks like* a connection error — so without care, stop would have resurrected the very turn you cancelled. Aborted turns are now excluded from `retryIndefinitelyWhen` and marked permanent in `PERMANENT_MESSAGE_PATTERNS`. And aborts are no longer treated as failures: `send-message.ts` and `queued-message-interrupt.ts` return quietly instead of marking the worker `error` and failing the run — otherwise every stop would have painted a red banner.

**Delete** aborts every live turn *before* `waitForConversationBackgroundTasks`, which is what makes that wait bounded rather than hostage to an agent that never acknowledges. To be explicit: **stop does not delete anything** — deletion only happens on the delete endpoint you choose to call.

## Tests

New `tests/server/conversations/worker-turn-abort.test.ts` (5 tests) proves it against a turn that *never finishes on its own* — the wedged-agent case:

- aborts in **<200ms** and the replacement turn starts in **<200ms**
- the ambient signal reaches nested callers
- abort is idempotent

Two existing tests encoded the old behaviour and I rewrote them rather than worked around them:
- `queued-message-interrupt`: "keeps the queued message pending when cancelling the turn fails" → **"still steers when the agent-side cancel fails"**. That test *was* the 502 veto you were hitting.
- `bridge-client`: mock updated for the two new exports.

## Not done

Two things I flagged earlier and did not act on, both yours to call: reverting/cleaning `2e6d9a8` on GitHub, and disabling `auto_commit_milestones`/`push_on_commit` for runs whose project path is the OmniHarness repo itself. That run pushed to `master` autonomously while failing auth — I'd turn it off before it happens again.

import { execFileSync } from "child_process";
import { mkdirSync, mkdtempSync, writeFileSync } from "fs";
import { tmpdir } from "os";
import path from "path";
import { beforeEach, describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { db } from "@/server/db";
import { executionEvents, plans, runs } from "@/server/db/schema";
import { captureGitBaseline } from "@/server/git/auto-commit";
import { runMilestoneAutoCommit } from "@/server/git/run-auto-commit";

function git(cwd: string, args: string[]) {
  return execFileSync("git", args, {
    cwd,
    encoding: "utf8",
    stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"],
  }).trim();
}

function createRepo(name: string) {
  const repo = mkdtempSync(path.join(tmpdir(), `omni-${name}-`));
  git(repo, ["init"]);
  git(repo, ["config", "user.name", "OmniHarness Test"]);
  git(repo, ["config", "user.email", "omni@example.test"]);
  writeFileSync(path.join(repo, "README.md"), "# Test\n");
  git(repo, ["add", "README.md"]);
  git(repo, ["commit", "-m", "initial"]);
  return repo;
}

describe("runMilestoneAutoCommit", () => {
  beforeEach(async () => {
    await db.delete(executionEvents);
    await db.delete(runs);
    await db.delete(plans);
  });

  it("creates a milestone commit for completed direct runs", async () => {
    const repo = createRepo("direct-run-auto-commit");
    const baseline = captureGitBaseline(repo);
    writeFileSync(path.join(repo, "feature.txt"), "implemented\n");
    const now = new Date();
    await db.insert(plans).values({
      id: "plan-direct-commit",
      path: "vibes/ad-hoc/direct-commit.md",
      status: "running",
      createdAt: now,
      updatedAt: now,
    });
    await db.insert(runs).values({
      id: "run-direct-commit",
      planId: "plan-direct-commit",
      mode: "direct",
      projectPath: repo,
      title: "Direct implementation",
      status: "done",
      autoCommitMilestones: true,
      pushOnCommit: false,
      gitBaselineJson: JSON.stringify(baseline),
      createdAt: now,
      updatedAt: now,
    });

    const result = await runMilestoneAutoCommit("run-direct-commit", "Direct run completed.");

    expect(result?.status).toBe("created");
    expect(git(repo, ["log", "-1", "--pretty=%s"])).toBe("Direct implementation");
    expect(git(repo, ["log", "-1", "--pretty=%B"])).not.toContain("OmniHarness");
    const event = await db.select().from(executionEvents).get();
    expect(event?.eventType).toBe("auto_commit_created");
  });

  it("emits created instead of failed for unstaged tracked src path modifications", async () => {
    const repo = createRepo("direct-run-auto-commit-src-path");
    const trackedPath = path.join(repo, "src", "app", "(public)", "(marketing)", "page.tsx");
    mkdirSync(path.dirname(trackedPath), { recursive: true });

## Claude · 2026-08-03T08:01:21.476Z

**373 files, 2411 tests passing, all four typecheck projects clean.** GitHub untouched.

## Only a healthy conversation can commit or push

`runMilestoneAutoCommit` checked exactly two things before committing: the run's mode and that it had a `projectPath`. Nothing about whether the conversation was alive. That's how a suspended-account run committed your whole working tree — auto-resume replayed it, the replay produced terminal-looking output, `updateDirectRunStatusFromWorkerOutput` saw `done`, and the commit fired.

The gate is now in `runMilestoneAutoCommit`, so it covers both call sites (direct runs *and* the supervisor). It declines when:

- the run is `failed`, `needs_recovery`, `cancelled`, or `quota_waiting`
- `failedAt` is set
- `lastError` is a **non-transient** error — this reuses `isTransientSupervisorError`, so it's the same classifier I fixed earlier today. A revoked token or suspended account now blocks the commit; an `ECONNRESET` doesn't
- a recovery incident is still `open`/`recovering`/`needs_user`
- no worker is in a healthy state

It's an affirmative health check, not the absence of an objection — committing is outward-facing, so silence isn't consent.

## You see what it did, and what it didn't

The five inline conversation events already existed and render correctly (`INLINE_CONVERSATION_EVENT_TYPES` in `utils.ts`). Two gaps closed:

- **A blocked commit now says so.** `auto_commit_skipped` with the actual reason — *"Auto-commit skipped: the conversation is failed"* — plus `wouldHavePushed`, so you can see a push was configured and withheld.
- **A commit that was supposed to push but didn't attempt one is no longer silent.** If `pushOnCommit` is set and `pushStatus` came back `not_requested`, that produced *no event at all* — which reads in the conversation as "pushed". It now emits `auto_commit_push_failed` with `push_not_attempted`.

So every path is now visible: committed, pushed, push failed, push not attempted, skipped-and-why.

## Tests

Five new tests in `tests/server/git/run-auto-commit.test.ts`, one of which replays this morning verbatim — a run with `status: failed`, `lastError: "…403 Account suspended"`, `pushOnCommit: true`, a dirty file in the tree — and asserts `HEAD` is **unchanged** and the conversation gets an `auto_commit_skipped` event. Plus: recovery-still-open blocks, no-healthy-worker blocks, healthy still commits, and a transient `ECONNRESET` still commits (so the gate doesn't over-block).

One note on the run: `tests/interface/vite-build.test.ts` failed on the first full-suite pass and passed both in isolation and on a clean re-run. It shells out to a real `pnpm` vite build, so it's contention under parallel load — unrelated to these changes, but I'm flagging it rather than quietly re-running until green.

  const handleProjectDrop = (event: React.DragEvent<HTMLElement>, targetPath: string) => {
    const draggedPath = event.dataTransfer.getData(PROJECT_DRAG_DATA_TYPE)
      || event.dataTransfer.getData("text/plain");
    if (!draggedPath || draggedPath === targetPath) {
      return;
    }

    event.preventDefault();
    event.stopPropagation();
    const rect = event.currentTarget.getBoundingClientRect();
    const placement: ProjectDropPlacement = event.clientY > rect.top + rect.height / 2 ? "after" : "before";
    onReorderProjects(draggedPath, targetPath, placement);
  };

  return (
    <>
      {groups.map((group) => {
        const projectOpen = !collapsedProjectPaths.has(group.path);
        const canDragProject = canReorderProjects && group.path !== "other";
        const visibleSessionCount = visibleProjectSessionCounts[group.path] ?? PROJECT_SESSION_DISPLAY_BATCH_SIZE;
        const visibleRuns = group.runs.slice(0, visibleSessionCount);
        const hiddenSessionCount = Math.max(0, group.runs.length - visibleRuns.length);
        const nextSessionBatchCount = Math.min(PROJECT_SESSION_DISPLAY_BATCH_SIZE, hiddenSessionCount);

        return (
          <Collapsible
            key={group.path}
            open={projectOpen}
            onOpenChange={(open) => onProjectOpenChange(group.path, open)}
          >
            <div
              data-project-drag-row="true"
              data-project-path={group.path}
              className="group mb-1 flex items-center justify-between gap-0.5 rounded px-2 hover:bg-muted/30"
              onDragOver={(event) => {
                if (!canDragProject) return;
                event.preventDefault();
                event.dataTransfer.dropEffect = "move";
              }}
              onDrop={(event) => handleProjectDrop(event, group.path)}
            >
              {canDragProject ? (
                <span
                  draggable={canDragProject}
                  className="flex h-6 w-4 shrink-0 cursor-grab items-center justify-center text-muted-foreground/55 transition-colors hover:text-muted-foreground active:cursor-grabbing"
                  aria-label={t("conversation.sidebar.dragProject", { project: group.name })}
                  title={t("conversation.sidebar.dragProject", { project: group.name })}
                  onClick={(event) => event.stopPropagation()}
                  onDragStart={(event) => {
                    event.dataTransfer.effectAllowed = "move";
                    event.dataTransfer.setData(PROJECT_DRAG_DATA_TYPE, group.path);
                    event.dataTransfer.setData("text/plain", group.path);
                    const projectDragRow = event.currentTarget.closest<HTMLElement>('[data-project-drag-row="true"]');
                    if (projectDragRow) {
                      event.dataTransfer.setDragImage(projectDragRow, 16, projectDragRow.offsetHeight / 2);
                    }
                  }}
                >
                  <GripVertical className="h-3.5 w-3.5" aria-hidden="true" />
                </span>
              ) : null}
              <CollapsibleTrigger className="flex flex-1 items-center gap-2 py-1 text-sm font-medium text-muted-foreground transition-colors hover:text-foreground">
                <Folder className="h-4 w-4 shrink-0 text-primary/70" />
                <span className="truncate">{group.name}</span>
                <ChevronDown
                  className={cn("ml-auto h-3.5 w-3.5 shrink-0 transition-transform duration-150 ease-out", projectOpen && "rotate-180")}
                  aria-hidden="true"
                />
              </CollapsibleTrigger>

              {group.path !== "other" ? (
                <div className="flex shrink-0 items-center gap-0.5">
                  <Button
                    variant="ghost"
                    size="icon"
                    className="h-6 w-6 text-muted-foreground opacity-100 hover:text-foreground lg:opacity-0 lg:group-hover:opacity-100"
                    title={t("conversation.sidebar.newConversationInProject", { project: group.name })}
                    onClick={() => beginConversationInProject(group.path)}
                  >
                    <Plus className="h-3.5 w-3.5" />
                  </Button>
                  <DropdownMenu>
                    <DropdownMenuTrigger className="inline-flex h-6 w-6 shrink-0 items-center justify-center rounded-md text-sm font-medium text-muted-foreground opacity-100 transition-colors ring-offset-background hover:bg-accent hover:text-foreground focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring focus-visible:ring-offset-2 disabled:pointer-events-none disabled:opacity-50 lg:opacity-0 lg:group-hover:opacity-100">

                      <DropdownMenuItem

                      >
                        <GitCommitHorizontal className="mr-2 h-4 w-4" /> {t("commit.menu.commitProjectNow")}

                      </DropdownMenuItem>

export type StateUpdate<T> = T | ((current: T) => T);
export type StateListener = () => void;

export class StateManager<TState> {
  private state: TState;
  private readonly initialState: TState;
  private readonly listeners = new Set<StateListener>();

  constructor(initialState: TState) {
    this.state = initialState;
    this.initialState = initialState;
  }

  getSnapshot() {
    return this.state;
  }

  getInitialSnapshot() {
    return this.initialState;
  }

  subscribe(listener: StateListener) {
    this.listeners.add(listener);
    return () => {
      this.listeners.delete(listener);
    };
  }

  update(updater: StateUpdate<TState>, notify = true) {
    const nextState = typeof updater === "function"
      ? (updater as (current: TState) => TState)(this.state)
      : updater;

    if (Object.is(nextState, this.state)) {
      return this.state;
    }

    this.state = nextState;
    if (notify) {
      this.listeners.forEach((listener) => listener());
    }
    return this.state;
  }

  patch(patch: Partial<TState> | ((current: TState) => Partial<TState>), notify = true) {
    return this.update((current) => ({
      ...current,
      ...(typeof patch === "function" ? patch(current) : patch),
    }), notify);
  }

"use client";

import { useCallback, useRef, useSyncExternalStore } from "react";
import type { StateManager } from "@/lib/state-manager";

export function useManagerSnapshot<TState>(manager: StateManager<TState>) {
  return useSyncExternalStore(
    useCallback((listener) => manager.subscribe(listener), [manager]),
    useCallback(() => manager.getSnapshot(), [manager]),
    useCallback(() => manager.getInitialSnapshot(), [manager]),
  );
}

export function shallowEqualRecord<TRecord extends Record<string, unknown>>(
  left: TRecord,
  right: TRecord,
) {
  if (Object.is(left, right)) {
    return true;
  }

  const leftKeys = Object.keys(left);
  const rightKeys = Object.keys(right);
  if (leftKeys.length !== rightKeys.length) {
    return false;
  }

  return leftKeys.every((key) => Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(right, key)
    && Object.is(left[key], right[key]));
}

## Claude · 2026-08-03T08:11:14.286Z

**373 files, 2411 tests, 4 typecheck projects, 0 lint errors.** (The 33 warnings are pre-existing, all in test files.)

## Drag-and-drop: you now see where it lands

`onDragOver` did nothing but `preventDefault()` — placement was computed *only at drop time* from `clientY`, so there was genuinely no feedback to give. Now:

- A **blue insertion line** (`bg-sky-500`) with a leading dot renders at the row's top or bottom edge, following your cursor across the midpoint. It's inset `inset-x-1` and sits on the row boundary (`-top-px`/`-bottom-px`) so it reads as "here, between these two" rather than as an underline belonging to one row.
- The row being dragged **dims to 40%**, so the source is obvious.
- Two edge cases that would otherwise look broken: the dragged row never draws a line against *itself*, and `onDragEnd` clears the state when you cancel with Esc or drop outside any row (`drop` never fires in those cases).

One subtlety worth naming: `dataTransfer` payloads are unreadable during `dragover` for security reasons, so the dragged path has to be tracked separately — reading it back during the hover is not an option.

I initially wrote this with `useState` and your own test caught it: `tests/ui/react-best-practices.test.ts` enforces *"keeps frontend state in Manager classes instead of component useState"*. Rewrote it as a `ProjectDragManager extends StateManager` consumed via `useManagerSnapshot`, matching `ConversationSidebarHydrationManager` in the same file.

## The worker question card

Your read on the type was exactly right. Measured from the old markup:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Eyebrow ("Worker question") | 12px | **11px** |
| The question itself | 14px | **15px, semibold** |
| Option labels | 14px | **13px** |

The question was tied with the options and *smaller* than nothing — the eyebrow was the only thing styled as a heading, at the smallest size. Now it descends properly: question → options → eyebrow.

**The option boxes are gone.** Each option was `rounded-xl border p-3` with its own `bg-background/70` — a stack of competing cards for what is usually two or three words. They're now plain rows with hover and a soft `bg-sky-500/10` tint when selected. The radio/checkbox *is* the affordance; it doesn't need a box drawn around it.

**The card now belongs to the app.** It was a full sky wash (`bg-sky-500/[0.055]`, `rounded-2xl`, `border-sky-500/25`) unlike any other surface. It's now the standard `bg-card` + `ring-1 ring-foreground/10` used by the `Card` primitive, with the sky accent carried by a single 3px left edge — so it still reads as "question" at a glance without shouting. Tabs, inputs, and footer buttons were pulled to the same 13px scale, and the buttons lost their heavy borders in favour of a ghost/primary pair.

I verified the actual rendered markup rather than trusting the diff — confirmed the 15/13/11px hierarchy and that no option carries a border or background class.

I left `InlinePermission.tsx` alone since you didn't mention it, but it shares the old pattern (amber wash, 12px eyebrow). Happy to bring it onto the same system so the two inline cards match — say the word.

So a superseded delivery is\n   * released here instead:\n   *\n   * - `appended: false` — nothing was written yet, so the row goes back to\n   *   `pending`: the message is still queued, visible, and retryable.\n   * - `appended: true` — the message is already in the transcript and its id is\n   *   the primary key of the `messages` row, so re-delivering it would collide.\n   *   The row is closed as delivered and the supersede is recorded.\n   */\n  const releaseSupersededRow = async (appended: boolean) => {\n    if (await queuedRowStatus(record.id) !== \"delivering\") {\n      return;\n    }\n    const now = new Date();\n    await db.update(queuedConversationMessages).set({\n      status: appended ? \"delivered\" : \"pending\",\n      lastError: null,\n      updatedAt: now,\n      ...(appended ? { deliveredAt: now } : {}),\n    }).where(eq(queuedConversationMessages.id, record.id));\n    await recordExecutionEvent({\n      runId,\n      workerId: worker.id,\n      eventType: \"queued_message_interrupt_superseded\",\n      details: {\n        summary: appended\n          ? `A newer turn took over after ${worker.id} already received this message.`\n          : `Requeued the message for ${worker.id} because a newer turn took over before it was sent.`,\n        queuedMessageId: record.id,\n        appendedToTranscript: appended,\n        source,\n      },\n    });\n  };\n\n  const isStillCurrent = async (appended = false) => {\n    if (await queuedRowStatus(record.id) !== \"delivering\") {\n      return false;\n    }\n    if (await isWorkerTurnGenerationCurrent(worker.id, generation)) {\n      return true;\n    }\n    await releaseSupersededRow(appended);\n    return false;\n  };"
}

export async function requeueRecoverableQueuedMessages(args: {
  runId: string;
  workerId?: string | null;
}) {
  const records = await db.select()
    .from(queuedConversationMessages)
    .where(eq(queuedConversationMessages.runId, args.runId));

  const recoverableIds = records
    .filter((record) => (
      (record.status === "failed" || record.status === "delivering")
      && isRecoverableAgentMissingError(record.lastError)
      && (!args.workerId || !record.targetWorkerId || record.targetWorkerId === args.workerId)
    ))
    .map((record) => record.id);

  if (recoverableIds.length === 0) {
    return 0;
  }

  await db.update(queuedConversationMessages).set({
    status: "pending",
    action: "queue",
    targetWorkerId: null,
    lastError: null,
    updatedAt: new Date(),
    deliveredAt: null,
  }).where(inArray(queuedConversationMessages.id, recoverableIds));

No such delivery\n * survives a process restart, so any row still marked `delivering` at boot is\n * orphaned: its owner died mid-flight. Left alone it dangles forever — and\n * since `delivering` rows are no longer listed as queued, it would dangle\n * invisibly. Reclaim them as `pending` so the user's message comes back.\n */\nexport async function reclaimOrphanedDeliveringMessages() {\n  const orphaned = await db\n    .select({ id: queuedConversationMessages.id, runId: queuedConversationMessages.runId })\n    .from(queuedConversationMessages)\n    .where(eq(queuedConversationMessages.status, \"delivering\"));\n  if (orphaned.length === 0) {\n    return 0;\n  }\n\n  const now = new Date();\n  await db.update(queuedConversationMessages).set({\n    status: \"pending\",\n    lastError: null,\n    updatedAt: now,\n    deliveredAt: null,\n  }).where(inArray(queuedConversationMessages.id, orphaned.map((record) => record.id)));\n\n  for (const record of orphaned) {\n    await insertQueueExecutionEvent(record.runId, \"queued_message_reclaimed\", {\n      summary: \"Requeued a message whose delivery was interrupted by a restart.\",\n      queuedMessageId: record.id,\n    });\n  }\n  notifyEventStreamSubscribers();\n  return orphaned.length;\n}\n\nexport async function createQueuedConversationMessage({"
}

## Claude · 2026-08-03T08:19:39.592Z

**373 files, 2415 tests, 4 typecheck projects, 0 lint errors.**

## It wasn't stale code — the row really was still in the queue

Your instinct to doubt it was right, but the cause was real. I found row `65ad444c` sitting at `status = 'delivering'`, and both queue readers treat that as *still queued*:

```
events.ts:165          inArray(status, ["pending", "delivering"])
queued-messages.ts:444 status === "pending" || status === "delivering"
```

The row only flips to `delivered` **after `askAgent` resolves** — i.e. after the agent's entire turn finishes. So your force-send worked, the message went into the transcript immediately… and then sat in the queue for the whole turn. That row finally cleared at 10:14:24, three minutes after you sent it. Exactly what you described.

**Fix: only `pending` is queued.** Once a message is dispatched (`delivering`), it has left the queue — it's with the worker and visible in the transcript. If dispatch fails, the existing code puts it back to `pending` and it reappears, which is the honest signal.

## The leak that fix would have hidden

Making `delivering` invisible is only safe if a row can never get *stuck* there. It could, in two ways:

**Superseded deliveries dangled.** Four guards in `deliverInterruptedQueuedMessage` did a bare `return` when a newer turn took over, leaving the row `delivering` with nothing to ever resolve it. Under the old listing that was visible clutter; under the new one it'd be a message that silently vanished. They now release the row:
- superseded *before* the message was written → back to `pending` (queued, visible, retryable)
- superseded *after* → closed as `delivered`, since the message id is the `messages` primary key and re-delivering would collide

Either way an event is recorded, and the guard that protects the newer delivery still runs **before** `persistDeliveredWorkerResponse` — I verified the stale response still never reaches the transcript.

**A restart orphaned them.** No in-process delivery survives a restart, so any row still `delivering` at boot is dead. `reclaimOrphanedDeliveringMessages()` now runs in `startRunnerProcess` right after `dbReady` and returns them to `pending`. The existing `requeueRecoverableQueuedMessages` didn't cover this — it only matches rows whose `lastError` is an agent-missing error, and an orphan has `lastError: null`.

## One test changed, and I want to flag why

`"does not let a stale interrupted-turn completion overwrite a newer delivery"` asserted `storedFirst.status).not.toBe("delivered")`. That was using "didn't reach delivered" as a proxy for "didn't do a terminal write" — but the state it was actually asserting was the dangling `delivering`. Since the agent genuinely did receive that message, `delivered` is the truthful outcome. I replaced the proxy with the invariants that matter: the late output never reaches the transcript, the row is not left `delivering`, the queue is empty, and a supersede event exists. Stronger, not weaker.

## Note on your running instance

Your runner has been up since **05:30** — none of today's changes are live in it. That includes the instant stop/steer work from earlier. You'll need to restart it to get any of this.

Start it with `pnpm restart:control`.\",\n    };\n  }\n\n  try {\n    const response = await doFetch(`http://127.0.0.1:${config.port}/restart-current`, {\n      method: \"POST\",\n      headers: {\n        Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`,\n        Accept: \"application/json\",\n      },\n      signal: AbortSignal.timeout(CONTROL_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS),\n    });\n\n    if (response.status === 401 || response.status === 403) {\n      return {\n        ok: false,\n        code: \"control_unauthorized\",\n        message: \"The restart control service rejected this runner's token.\",\n      };\n    }\n\n    if (!response.ok) {\n      const detail = await response.text().catch(() => \"\");\n      return {\n        ok: false,\n        code: \"control_failed\",\n        message: `The restart control service returned ${response.status}${detail ? `: ${detail.slice(0, 200)}` : \".\"}`,\n      };\n    }\n\n    const payload = await response.json().catch(() => ({})) as {\n      pid?: unknown;\n      mode?: unknown;\n      startedAt?: unknown;\n    };\n    return {\n      ok: true,\n      pid: typeof payload.pid === \"number\" ? payload.pid : null,\n      mode: typeof payload.mode === \"string\" ? payload.mode : null,\n      startedAt: typeof payload.startedAt === \"number\" ? payload.startedAt : null,\n    };\n  } catch (error) {\n    if (isConnectionRefused(error)) {\n      return {\n        ok: false,\n        code: \"control_unavailable\",\n        message: `No restart control service is listening on port ${config.port}. ## Claude · 2026-08-03T08:40:07.593Z

Restart done, and the UI button is built. **374 files, 2420 tests, 0 lint errors, all typechecks clean.**

## The restart

New runner PID **65533** at 10:32:02, bridge relistening on 7800. I used the restart-control service rather than killing the process, so it came back on its own. Verified after boot: **0 orphaned `delivering` rows**, queue empty. The reclaim logged nothing because there was nothing to reclaim — that stuck row had already resolved at 10:14.

Three turns were live and got interrupted (`66a4470d65c5`, `5799b75efb7d`, `0e5325b25743`); recovery picks those up. Since the runner runs through `tsx` with no build step, everything from today is now live.

## "Restart server" in the UI

One constraint shaped the whole design: **a runner cannot restart itself.** The process serving the request is the one that has to die — it could never send a response or bring itself back. That's why the restart-control service is a separate process on :3099, and why I couldn't just add a handler that restarts in place.

So the button proxies. The browser can't call :3099 directly (different origin, and the token is a `0600` file on disk), so the runner reads the token and forwards:

- `POST /api/runner/restart` → `requireApiSession` with `enforceSameOrigin: true`, matching `rekey`. Restarting kills every in-flight turn on that machine, so a bearer token from elsewhere doesn't get to trigger it.
- Returns **202** — the control service has accepted the job; the response goes out before this process dies.
- Failures are distinguished rather than lumped together: `control_unavailable` (503, service down or no token — tells you to run `pnpm restart:control`), `control_unauthorized` (502, stale token), `control_failed`. If the control service isn't running you get a real explanation instead of a generic error.
- Both outcomes write an auth-audit event.

**UI:** "Restart server" sits right after "Manage sessions" in the runner dropdown, exactly where you suggested, with a destructive-styled confirm dialog. It only appears for the same-origin runner — you can't restart a remote server you've merely connected to. The dialog copy says plainly that turns are interrupted and recovered, and that **nothing is deleted**. Keys added to all 9 locales (purely additive — `9 files, 63 insertions, 0 deletions`).

## Two guardrails caught me, correctly

Adding a route isn't a one-liner in this repo, by design:

1. `tests/runtime/route-contract-fixture.test.ts` — the route must be declared in `routes.v1.json`.
2. `tests/shared/api-revision.test.ts` — the fixture's fingerprint is pinned in `ROUTE_CONTRACT_DECLARATION`, so a route can't change without someone classifying the change. I updated the fingerprint and left `classification: "additive-capability"`, `capability: "runner_administration"`, and `apiRevision: 1` alone — an older client simply never calls the new route.

Tests: 4 new in `tests/server/runner/restart-request.test.ts` covering token forwarding, control-service-down, missing token, and rejected token.

One thing to know: the button depends on the restart-control service running. Yours is up (PID 2879), but it's started separately via `pnpm restart:control` — if it's not running, the UI will now tell you so explicitly rather than failing opaquely.
